title: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 1 (Paper 2) - Christian Religious Studies - The Ministry of Jesus Christ
exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 1 (Paper 2)
subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: By whom and in which river was Jesus Christ baptized?
options: By Peter in the Sea of Galilee
By John the Baptist in the River Jordan
By Zechariah in the River Nile
By Nicodemus at the Pool of Siloam
questions.explain: Jesus came from Galilee to the **Jordan River** to be baptized by **John the Baptist**. (Matthew 3:13)
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 1 (Paper 2)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: Which three supernatural events occurred immediately after Jesus was baptized and came up out of the water?
options: An earthquake, the temple veil tore, and graves opened.
The water turned to blood, darkness covered the earth, and fire fell.
The heavens opened, the Spirit of God descended like a dove, and a voice spoke from heaven.
Angels sang, a star appeared, and wise men visited.
questions.explain:
Matthew 3:16-17 outlines three distinct events: 
1. The heavens were opened. 
2. The Spirit of God descended like a dove. 
3. A voice from heaven spoke.
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 1 (Paper 2)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: During Jesus' baptism, the voice from heaven declared: *"This is my beloved Son..."* How did the statement conclude?
options: "...listen to Him carefully."
"...with whom I am well pleased."
"...who will save the world from sin."
"...He is the king of Israel."
questions.explain: The full declaration from the voice in heaven was: *"This is my beloved Son, with whom I am well pleased."* (Matthew 3:17)
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 1 (Paper 2)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: What is the primary significance of baptism in the life of a modern Christian?
options: It makes a person immune to sickness and temptation.
It is a requirement to become a community leader.
It is a public declaration of faith, symbolizing the washing away of sins and new life in Christ.
It replaces the need for daily prayer and reading the Bible.
questions.explain: Baptism serves as a public testimony of a believer's faith. It symbolically represents dying to one's old sinful life and rising to walk in the newness of life with Christ.
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 1 (Paper 2)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: According to the synoptic gospels, what led Jesus into the wilderness where he was tempted by the devil?
options: He ran away to hide from King Herod.
He was led up by the Holy Spirit.
He went to look for his lost sheep.
His disciples encouraged him to go on a retreat.
questions.explain: Matthew 4:1 explicitly states: *"Then Jesus was led up by the Spirit into the wilderness to be tempted by the devil."*
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 1 (Paper 2)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: After Jesus had fasted for forty days and forty nights, what was the very first temptation presented to Him by Satan?
options: To throw himself down from the pinnacle of the temple
To bow down and worship the devil
To turn stones into bread to satisfy his hunger
To turn water into wine to demonstrate his power
questions.explain: Knowing Jesus was hungry, the tempter came and said to him, "If you are the Son of God, command these stones to become loaves of bread." (Matthew 4:3)
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 1 (Paper 2)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: How did Jesus reply to the devil's temptation to turn stones into bread?
options: "Get behind me, Satan!"
"Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that comes from the mouth of God."
"You shall not put the Lord your God to the test."
"My food is to do the will of him who sent me."
questions.explain: Jesus answered by quoting Deuteronomy 8:3, emphasizing spiritual sustenance over physical desires: *"Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that comes from the mouth of God."*
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 1 (Paper 2)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: When Satan offered Jesus all the kingdoms of the world and their glory, what condition did the devil attach to this offer?
options: Jesus must perform a miracle for the devil.
Jesus must fall down and worship him.
Jesus must jump from the highest mountain.
Jesus must deny the existence of God.
questions.explain: Satan took him to a very high mountain and showed him all the kingdoms. He said, "All these I will give you, if you will fall down and worship me." (Matthew 4:9)
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 1 (Paper 2)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: Based on Jesus' victory over Satan, which of the following represents the most biblical ways for a Christian to overcome temptations today?
options: Avoiding the outside world and completely isolating oneself
Seeking revenge against those who cause the temptation
Relying on prayer, being strong in faith, and applying the word of God
Giving in to the temptation once so that it will go away
questions.explain: Jesus overcame temptation by relying on the Scriptures (quoting God's word). The syllabus also highlights **prayer** and **being strong in faith** as the fundamental ways Christians overcome temptation today.
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 1 (Paper 2)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: Who were the first two disciples that Jesus called while walking by the Sea of Galilee?
options: James and John
Philip and Bartholomew
Matthew and Thomas
Simon (Peter) and his brother Andrew
questions.explain: Matthew 4:18 states: "While walking by the Sea of Galilee, he saw two brothers, Simon (who is called Peter) and Andrew his brother, casting a net into the sea, for they were fishermen."
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 1 (Paper 2)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: When calling his first disciples, Jesus used a metaphor related to their occupation as fishermen. What did He promise to make them?
options: Commanders of angels
Fishers of men
Kings of the sea
Shepherds of the flock
questions.explain: Jesus said to Peter and Andrew, > "Follow me, and I will make you **fishers of men**." (Matthew 4:19). He used their physical occupation to explain their new spiritual mission.
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 1 (Paper 2)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: Immediately after calling Peter and Andrew, Jesus saw two other brothers in a boat with their father mending their nets. Who were they?
options: James the son of Zebedee and his brother John
Judas Iscariot and Simon the Zealot
Paul and Silas
Moses and Aaron
questions.explain: Matthew 4:21 reads: "And going on from there he saw two other brothers, James the son of Zebedee and John his brother, in the boat with Zebedee their father, mending their nets, and he called them."
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 1 (Paper 2)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: In Luke 5:1-11, before calling Peter to be a disciple, Jesus performed a miracle that deeply impacted him. What was this miracle?
options: Jesus calmed a violent storm that threatened their boat.
Jesus healed Peter's mother-in-law.
Jesus provided a miraculous catch of fish after Peter had toiled all night and caught nothing.
Jesus turned a boat full of water into wine.
questions.explain: After Peter allowed Jesus to preach from his boat, Jesus instructed him to let down his nets. Despite catching nothing all night, the catch was so large that the nets began to tear, prompting Peter to fall at Jesus' knees.
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 1 (Paper 2)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: In teaching what it takes to be a disciple, Jesus said to a man who wanted to say farewell to his family first: "No one who puts his hand to the plow and looks back is ________."
options: Able to see the harvest
Fit for the kingdom of God
Worthy to be a fisherman
Going to find peace
questions.explain: Luke 9:62 captures Jesus' teaching on total commitment to discipleship: *"Jesus said to him, 'No one who puts his hand to the plow and looks back is fit for the kingdom of God.'"*
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 1 (Paper 2)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: When Jesus sent out the twelve apostles, he instructed them NOT to go among the Gentiles or to any town of the Samaritans. According to Matthew 10:5-6, to whom were they told to go instead?
options: The kings and rulers of the earth
The lost sheep of the house of Israel
The Roman soldiers stationed in Judea
The ends of the earth
questions.explain: In His initial commission to the Twelve, Jesus strictly bounded their mission, saying: "Go nowhere among the Gentiles and enter no town of the Samaritans, but go rather to the lost sheep of the house of Israel." (Matthew 10:5-6)
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 1 (Paper 2)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: What specific instructions did Jesus give the apostles regarding what to pack for their evangelism journey in Matthew 10?
options: They should carry extra gold and silver for emergencies.
They should take no gold, silver, copper, or extra tunic.
They should ride on horses to travel faster between villages.
They must carry a sword to protect themselves.
questions.explain: Jesus taught them to rely entirely on God's provision and the hospitality of the people they preached to, instructing them: "Acquire no gold or silver or copper for your belts, no knapsack for your journey, or two tunics or sandals or a staff." (Matthew 10:9-10)
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 1 (Paper 2)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: After the seventy disciples returned from their mission with joy, declaring that even demons submitted to them, what did Jesus tell them they should truly rejoice over? (Luke 10:17-20)
options: That they had become famous throughout all of Judea
That they had healed many sick people
That their names are written in heaven
That they were now immune to all illnesses
questions.explain: Jesus warned them against pride in spiritual power, saying: "Nevertheless, do not rejoice in this, that the spirits are subject to you, but rejoice that your names are written in heaven." (Luke 10:20)
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 1 (Paper 2)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: According to the Beatitudes taught by Jesus in the Sermon on the Mount, "Blessed are the merciful, for they shall ____________."
options: inherit the earth
see God
obtain mercy
be called sons of God
questions.explain: Matthew 5:7 states, "Blessed are the merciful, for they shall receive mercy" (or obtain mercy, depending on the translation).
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 1 (Paper 2)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: In the Sermon on the Mount (Matthew 5:13-16), Jesus called his disciples the "salt of the earth" and what other metaphor?
options: The stars of the sky
The light of the world
The shepherds of the flock
The kings of the nations
questions.explain: After declaring them the salt of the earth, Jesus immediately added, "You are the light of the world. A city set on a hill cannot be hidden." (Matthew 5:14)
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 1 (Paper 2)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: What was Jesus' main instruction regarding fasting in Matthew 6:16-18?
options: Fasting must be done publicly so others can learn from it.
Christians should never fast, they only need to pray.
Believers should wash their faces and not look gloomy, so their fasting is seen only by God.
Fasting is only required for priests and community leaders.
questions.explain: Jesus rebuked hypocrites who disfigured their faces to look hungry. He commanded, "But when you fast, anoint your head and wash your face, that your fasting may not be seen by others but by your Father who is in secret."
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 1 (Paper 2)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: In his teaching against the love of money, Jesus declared that "no one can serve two masters." Who are the two masters he referred to in Matthew 6:24?
options: God and the government
God and money
Angels and demons
The synagogue and the temple
questions.explain: Jesus clearly warned about divided loyalties, concluding the teaching with: "You cannot serve God and money" (some versions translate "money" as "mammon").
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 1 (Paper 2)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: To teach his followers not to worry about what they will eat or wear, which elements of nature did Jesus use as examples of God's provision? (Matthew 6:25-34)
options: The lions of the forest and the great cedar trees
The fish of the sea and the sand on the shore
The birds of the air and the lilies of the field
The sheep on the hills and the grass of the pasture
questions.explain: Jesus said, "Look at the birds of the air... your heavenly Father feeds them," and "Consider the lilies of the field, how they grow... even Solomon in all his glory was not arrayed like one of these."
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 1 (Paper 2)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: According to Matthew 13:34-35, why did Jesus often teach the crowds using parables?
options: To entertain the young children who followed him.
Because it was illegal to preach openly in the region of Galilee.
To fulfill prophecy and to reveal the secrets of the kingdom of heaven to his disciples while hiding them from unbelievers.
To prove to the Pharisees that he was a highly educated scholar.
questions.explain: Jesus explained to his disciples that it was granted to them to know the secrets of the kingdom, but not to the crowds. He spoke in parables to fulfill the prophecy: "I will open my mouth in parables; I will utter what has been hidden since the foundation of the world." (Matthew 13:35)
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 1 (Paper 2)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: In the Parable of the Sower (Matthew 13), what does the seed that fell among thorns represent?
options: Those who hear the word, but the cares of the world and the deceitfulness of riches choke it.
Those who receive the word with joy but fall away quickly during times of persecution.
Those who hear the word but do not understand it at all, so the evil one snatches it away.
Those who hear the word, understand it, and bear much fruit.
questions.explain: Jesus interpreted the parable, explaining: "As for what was sown among thorns, this is the one who hears the word, but the cares of the world and the deceitfulness of riches choke the word, and it proves unfruitful." (Matthew 13:22)
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 1 (Paper 2)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: In the Parable of the Prodigal Son (Luke 15:11-32), what humiliating job was the younger son forced to do after spending his inheritance and experiencing a severe famine?
options: He had to fetch water from a deep well all day.
He hired himself out to feed pigs in the fields.
He was forced into slavery making bricks for the governor.
He became a beggar at the gates of the temple.
questions.explain: After spending everything, a severe famine arose. "So he went and hired himself out to one of the citizens of that country, who sent him into his fields to feed pigs." This was particularly humiliating for a Jewish man.
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 1 (Paper 2)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: What critical mistake did the man make in the Parable of the Rich Fool (Luke 12:13-21)?
options: He refused to pay his legal taxes to Caesar.
He invested all his money in a barren plot of land.
He hoarded wealth for himself on earth but was not rich toward God.
He gave his money away to thieves and robbers.
questions.explain: The rich man planned to build bigger barns and rest for years, ignoring his spiritual state. God called him a fool, warning that his soul would be demanded that night. Jesus concluded: "So is the one who lays up treasure for himself and is not rich toward God."
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 1 (Paper 2)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: In the Parable of the Ten Virgins (Matthew 25:1-13), what action distinguished the five wise virgins from the five foolish ones?
options: The wise virgins managed to stay awake the entire night without sleeping.
The wise virgins took extra flasks of oil with their lamps.
The foolish virgins brought water instead of oil.
The foolish virgins left the venue to attend a different wedding.
questions.explain: All ten virgins fell asleep waiting, but the wise were prepared: "For when the foolish took their lamps, they took no oil with them, but the wise took flasks of oil with their lamps."
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 1 (Paper 2)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: The Parable of the Unforgiving Steward (Matthew 18:21-35) emphasizes the necessity of forgiveness. How did the king punish the servant who was forgiven a huge debt but refused to forgive his fellow servant's small debt?
options: The king demoted him to work in the fields.
The king gave him three more days to change his mind.
The king delivered him to the jailers until he should pay all his original debt.
The king sent him into permanent exile in a foreign land.
questions.explain: Because of his wicked lack of mercy, the master "delivered him to the jailers, until he should pay all his debt." Jesus warned that God will do the same if we do not forgive from our hearts.
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 1 (Paper 2)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: Where did Jesus perform His very first nature miracle by turning water into wine, as recorded in John 2:1-11?
options: At a funeral procession in Nain
At a wedding feast in Cana of Galilee
During the Passover in the temple at Jerusalem
During a storm on the Sea of Galilee
questions.explain: John 2 clearly identifies the setting of the miracle: "On the third day there was a wedding at Cana in Galilee, and the mother of Jesus was there... This, the first of his signs, Jesus did at Cana in Galilee, and manifested his glory."
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 1 (Paper 2)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: During a fierce windstorm on the sea (Mark 4:35-41), the disciples panicked while Jesus slept. After He awoke and rebuked the wind, what question did the disciples ask one another in awe?
options: "Who then is this, that even the wind and the sea obey him?"
"Why didn't we bring a larger boat for this journey?"
"When will we reach the other side safely?"
"Who will repair our torn fishing nets?"
questions.explain: Filled with great fear, they said to one another, "Who then is this, that even the wind and the sea obey him?" (Mark 4:41)
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 1 (Paper 2)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: In the miracle of the feeding of the five thousand, what was the initial amount of food provided to Jesus before He blessed and multiplied it?
options: Seven loaves of bread and a few small fish
Five loaves of bread and two fish
Two loaves of bread and five fish
Twelve baskets full of bread
questions.explain: They replied, "We have here only five loaves and two fish" (Matthew 14:17). *Note: The feeding of the 4,000 later involved seven loaves and a few small fish.*
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 1 (Paper 2)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: Why did Jesus marvel at the Roman Centurion who asked Him to heal his paralyzed servant (Matthew 8:5-13)?
options: Because the centurion offered Him a large bag of gold for the healing.
Because the centurion was an expert in Jewish religious laws.
Because the centurion believed Jesus only needed to speak a word from afar to heal the servant, demonstrating extraordinary faith.
Because the centurion agreed to abandon the Roman army to follow Him.
questions.explain: The centurion said, "Lord, I am not worthy to have you come under my roof, but only say the word, and my servant will be healed." Jesus marveled, saying He had not found such great faith in all of Israel.
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 1 (Paper 2)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: In an event showing Jesus subjecting Himself to religious laws (Matthew 17:24-27), He told Peter to pay the temple tax. How did Jesus provide the money for this tax?
options: He told Judas Iscariot to take the money from their shared moneybag.
He told Peter to cast a hook into the sea and find a coin in the mouth of the first fish caught.
He turned a piece of stone into a silver coin.
He asked a wealthy woman passing by to pay it on their behalf.
questions.explain: Jesus told Peter: "Go to the sea and cast a hook and take the first fish that comes up, and when you open its mouth you will find a shekel. Take that and give it to them for me and for yourself."
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 1 (Paper 2)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: In John 13:34-35, Jesus established a "new commandment" which represented love as the supreme law for His followers. What exactly was this commandment?
options: "That you memorize all the laws of Moses and recite them daily."
"That you sell all your possessions and give to the poor."
"That you love one another: just as I have loved you, you also are to love one another."
"That you build grand churches to honor my name."
questions.explain: Jesus elevated love above rigid laws, declaring: "A new commandment I give to you, that you love one another: just as I have loved you, you also are to love one another. By this all people will know that you are my disciples."
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 1 (Paper 2)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: In the miracle of Jesus walking on the water (Matthew 14:22-33), which of the disciples asked Jesus to command him to come out onto the water?
options: John
James
Peter
Andrew
questions.explain: When the disciples saw Jesus walking on the sea, Peter said, "Lord, if it is you, command me to come to you on the water." Jesus said, "Come," and Peter stepped out of the boat.
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 1 (Paper 2)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: When four men brought a paralyzed man to Jesus (Matthew 9:1-8), what controversial statement did Jesus make before healing him physically, which the scribes called blasphemy?
options: "Take up your bed and go home."
"Take heart, my son; your sins are forgiven."
"You will walk again in three days."
"Your faith is greater than that of the Pharisees."
questions.explain: Seeing their faith, Jesus told the paralytic, "Take heart, my son; your sins are forgiven." To prove He had authority on earth to forgive sins, He then healed the man's paralysis.
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 1 (Paper 2)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: In the healing of the Gerasene demoniac (Mark 5:1-20), the demons begged Jesus not to send them out of the country. Where did Jesus permit them to go instead?
options: Into a nearby lake to be drowned instantly
Into a flock of sheep grazing on the hillside
Into a large herd of pigs (swine)
Into the desert wasteland
questions.explain: The demons begged him, "Send us to the pigs; let us enter them." Jesus gave them permission, and the unclean spirits entered the herd of about two thousand pigs, which rushed down a steep bank into the sea.
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 1 (Paper 2)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: Jesus demonstrated His power over death at the town gate of Nain (Luke 7). Who did Jesus raise from the dead on this occasion?
options: Jairus's twelve-year-old daughter
The only son of a widow
His friend Lazarus
A Roman centurion's servant
questions.explain: As Jesus approached the town gate, a dead person was being carried out—the only son of his mother, and she was a widow. Jesus had compassion on her and commanded the young man to get up.
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 1 (Paper 2)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: Before Jesus raised Lazarus from the dead (John 11:1-45), how many days had Lazarus already been in the tomb?
options: Two days
Three days
Four days
Seven days
questions.explain: When Jesus finally arrived in Bethany, He found that Lazarus had already been in the tomb for **four days**. Martha even warned Jesus about the odor of decay, emphasizing the greatness of the miracle.
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 1 (Paper 2)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: In Matthew 5:17, Jesus clarified his attitude toward the Civil and Religious laws given to Moses. He stated, "Do not think that I have come to abolish the Law or the Prophets; I have not come to abolish them but to _________ them."
options: destroy
ignore
rewrite
fulfill
questions.explain: Jesus perfectly kept the requirements of the law and embodied its true meaning. His exact words were: "...I have not come to abolish them but to fulfill them."
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 1 (Paper 2)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: When the Pharisees tried to trap Jesus by asking if it was lawful to pay taxes to Caesar (Matthew 22:15-22), what wise answer did Jesus give?
options: "Therefore render to Caesar the things that are Caesar's, and to God the things that are God's."
"You must pay no tax, for God is your only King."
"Pay the temple tax first, and then whatever is left to Caesar."
"No one can serve two masters, therefore give everything to the poor."
questions.explain: After asking to see a coin and pointing out Caesar's image on it, Jesus replied, "Therefore render to Caesar the things that are Caesar's, and to God the things that are God's," perfectly navigating their political trap.
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 1 (Paper 2)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: Apostle Paul details the qualities of love in 1 Corinthians 13. According to this chapter, which of the following is **NOT** a characteristic of true Christian love?
options: Love is patient and kind.
Love does not insist on its own way.
Love bears all things, believes all things.
Love rejoices at wrongdoing.
questions.explain: 1 Corinthians 13:6 states clearly that love "does not rejoice at wrongdoing, but rejoices with the truth."
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 1 (Paper 2)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: In the Parable of the Wheat and the Tares (Weeds), what do the "tares" secretly sown in the field represent? (Matthew 13:36-43)
options: The angels of heaven
The sons of the evil one (Satan)
The religious leaders of Jerusalem
The poor and needy in society
questions.explain: Jesus explicitly interpreted this parable for His disciples: "The field is the world, and the good seed is the sons of the kingdom. The weeds are the sons of the evil one, and the enemy who sowed them is the devil."
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 1 (Paper 2)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: What is the central shared lesson in the parables of the Lost Sheep and the Lost Coin (Luke 15)?
options: That the wealthy must distribute all their money to the poor.
That God rejoices greatly over one sinner who repents.
That careless people will lose their earthly rewards.
That we must lock our doors against thieves.
questions.explain: Both parables end with a nearly identical summary from Jesus: "Just so, I tell you, there is joy before the angels of God over one sinner who repents."
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 1 (Paper 2)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
